exp1.detail: Experiment 1: matching task after learning phase, then 72 causality animations (physical causality emphasis; 6 practice animations). Matching task: 240 trials (2 blocks x 120; 4 conditions x 60), keys A/L counterbalanced, 100 ms stimulus, 1000 ms response window, 500 ms feedback. Data: 64 participants x 240 trials (author export 1_Matching_Task_1.csv from OSF e6hd7; columns participant/shape/RT/trial_type/block/resp_type; RT already in ms, negative values = early keypresses kept as-is). No trial-level raw export on OSF (author-processed format only; author export recorded the identity (you/stranger) but NOT the geometric shape). The paper reports the matching task only qualitatively ('robust self-prioritisation effect'); the direction was verified in the database (self-matching RT faster and more accurate than stranger-matching). Participants 8,16,22,31,58 excluded only from causality analyses (note_participants_removed.txt); matching-task data of all 64 participants retained. Shape-identity binding (circle=you vs square=you, counterbalanced) recovered per subject from the author's OrdineP1-40.xlsx files (experiment code, extracted 2026-08-30: 4 circle + 4 square alternating, subjects 1-40) and extrapolated by the same alternation for subjects 41-64 (Ordine files not uploaded; user-approved extrapolation, noted in CSV/Codebook); the raw data column ShapeIdentity keeps the author's identity values. Source: paper full text (PeerJ HTML) + OSF e6hd7; [P] paper, [D] data, [C] code.
